title: Efforts to Grow Manpower Talent for Key Sectors and to Groom Local Pipeline
what_it_is: Efforts to Grow Manpower Talent for Key Sectors and to Groom Local Pipeline

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework and Employment Pass questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about Fair Consideration Framework violations, regulatory actions, watchlist breaches, employment agencies, and Employment Pass holders by industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in the last five years, what is the number of instances where organisations have been found to have placed job advertisements without fairly considering applicants, violating the Fair Consideration Framework; and (b) what is the range of regulatory actions taken against such organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether there are plans to review the Employment Pass (EP) scheme to introduce a new dependency ratio ceiling for the bottom half of income earners among EP holders to encourage employers to enhance their Singaporean workforce by hiring and training more Singaporean talent and transferring skills from their foreign employees to the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many companies have been placed under the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices’ watchlist in 2021 due to possible breaches of the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF); (b) among those on the watchlist, how many have been found to have breached the FCF and debarred from hiring foreign workers and renewing their foreign workers’ work passes; and (c) how are employment agencies that breach the FCF dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in the past five years, how many Employment Pass (EP) holders have been employed in the technology and non-technology related industries respectively; and (b) whether useful information can be drawn from the number of EPs issued relative to the areas of skill and expectation mismatches and biasness in hiring practices.

sections.label: Employment Pass salary and COMPASS framework
sections.summary: The EP qualifying salary is benchmarked to the top one-third of local PMETs, and a points-based COMPASS will evaluate EP applications from 1 September 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, to benchmark the EP qualifying salary to the top one-third of our local Professionals, Managers, Executives and Technicians (PMETs) workforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And second, to introduce a new points-based Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) from 1 September 2023 to holistically evaluate EP applications for complementarity.

sections.label: ICT share of Employment Pass stock
sections.summary: In 2021, the ICT sector accounts for one-fifth of Singapore's Employment Pass stock.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In 2021, the ICT sector accounts for one-fifth of our EP stock.

sections.label: Resident PMET job proportion increase
sections.summary: The proportion of resident workers in PMET jobs rose from 55% in 2016 to 62% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The proportion of resident workers in PMET jobs increased from 55% in 2016 to 62% in 2021.

sections.label: Company Training Committees and NTUC grant
sections.summary: Companies are recommended to work with NTUC to set up Company Training Committees, with the Government setting aside a $70 million budget for the NTUC CTC grant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For instance, we recommend that companies work with NTUC to set up Company Training Committees (CTCs) to help drive business transformation and training plans – the Government has set aside a $70 million budget for the NTUC CTC grant.

sections.label: Legislating the recommendation
sections.summary: Work is now underway to enshrine this in legislation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Work is now underway to enshrine this in legislation.

sections.label: MOM employers under FCF
sections.summary: Since 2016, MOM has engaged more than 1,700 employers under FCF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Since 2016, MOM has engaged a total of more than 1,700 employers under FCF.

sections.label: MOM enforcement actions against companies
sections.summary: From 2017 to 2021, MOM took enforcement actions against approximately 300 companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In response to Mr Louis Chua and Mr Yip Hon Weng's questions, from 2017 to 2021, MOM took enforcement actions against approximately 300 companies.

sections.label: MOM action against culpable individuals
sections.summary: MOM can take action against culpable individuals and decision-makers for non-compliance with its rules and regulations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, MOM can take action against culpable individuals and decision-makers for non-compliance of MOM's rules and regulations.

sections.label: Employer duties and workplace fairness
sections.summary: Employers must comply with fair hiring laws and good HR practices, while the Tripartite Committee deliberates workplace fairness legislation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: All employers in Singapore must comply with not just the letter but with the spirit of our laws and regulations on fair hiring, and adopt good HR practices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The responsibility placed on employers as well as decision makers to uphold workplace fairness is also being discussed by the Tripartite Committee, which is deliberating the scope and design of workplace fairness legislation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: All our Government policies, all of our schemes as well as programmes, work together to achieve one goal – to create opportunities for locals, at all and every level of the workforce.

sections.label: Data on EP holders' salaries
sections.summary: Using the $30,000 salary criteria, a significant majority above that level are Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Perhaps, if Ms Tan could file a Parliamentary Question (PQ), we will try and get some of those data.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But, if you look at the proxy, if we use the $30,000 salary criteria of the ONE Pass mentioned at the last Parliamentary Sitting and given the fact that if you use the proportion of about 7,000 to 8,000 current EP holders who are at that level or above, a significant majority who have gone above that level are our Singaporeans.

sections.label: NRF Returning Singaporean Scientist Scheme
sections.summary: The National Research Foundation runs the Returning Singaporean Scientist Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Other agencies, like the National Research Foundation (NRF), also runs the Returning Singaporean Scientist Scheme (RSSS).

sections.label: COMPASS foundational criteria points
sections.summary: MOM is asked whether it can tighten COMPASS to require at least 10 points per foundational criterion and 50 points overall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can MOM tighten the COMPASS framework to require the candidate to obtain at least 10 points for each of the four foundational criteria and a minimum of 50 points overall?

sections.label: COMPASS framework start date
sections.summary: The COMPASS framework starts from 1 September 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As far as the COMPASS framework is concerned, we are starting from 1 September 2023.

sections.label: COMPASS implementation date
sections.summary: COMPASS will come into implementation on 1 September 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: COMPASS will come into implementation on 1 September 2023.

sections.label: Breaches, prosecution, career conversion regulator
sections.summary: IHRP may take corrective actions against HR professionals who breach manpower rules, MOM can prosecute false declarations, and a question asks who regulates career conversion programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If the HR professional has been found to have breached manpower rules and regulations, IHRP may subject the HR professional to corrective actions, such as counselling by senior certified professionals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In addition, MOM can also prosecute errant employers or key personnel who make false declarations that they have considered all candidates fairly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just one supplementary question – as we consider the criteria for which people without the academic qualifications may yet qualify for the career conversion programmes, who would be the regulator for that?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Would that be SkillsFuture Singapore or would it be dependent on the administrator of the programme?

sections.label: MOM help passing requirements
sections.summary: In that setting, MOM will work with the individual to see whether it can help the person pass these basic requirements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In that kind of setting, MOM will come in to work with the individual to see whether we can help the person pass these basic requirements.
